item: 1.1 — H11(a): log_sum sign of a non-finite log-likelihood
rule_implemented: In `log_sum` (inst/include/model_helpers.hpp): `operator+=(val)` now checks `val <= 0.0` first and, if so, sets a new private flag `zero_ = true` and returns without touching `prod_`/`sum_`; positive rates follow the unchanged product/fold logic. `result()` returns `-std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()` when `zero_` is set, otherwise plain `std::log(prod_) + sum_` — the old `signbit(sum_)`-based sign selection is removed entirely, so no sign is ever derived from `sum_`. NaN rates are not intercepted (`NaN <= 0` is false) and propagate as NaN through the product, as the plain formula would; +Inf rates yield a genuine +Inf. Only non-finite outcomes change: every finite path is bit-for-bit the same computation as before.

My branch had no commits and a clean tree, so I ran `git reset --hard f5f51ce` before doing anything; the commit's parent is main's HEAD. The merger should check whether the other d9ca72a-based agents did the same. Rule itself: implemented as stated, no deviations.

item: 1.2 — H11(c), H4: src/M_step.cpp objective() and M_step()
rule_implemented: In src/M_step.cpp: (1) nlopt_f_data now carries sum_w = std::accumulate over the weight vector handed to M_step() (i.e. over the trees passed, zeros included since they add nothing). (2) objective(): in the parallel_reduce loop, a tree with w[i] == 0.0 is skipped without evaluating loglik; if a weighted tree's loglik is not finite (std::isfinite false: -Inf, +Inf or NaN), the partial sum is set to -Inf (partials are therefore finite or -Inf, never NaN), and after the reduction a non-finite Q makes the objective return +Inf. (3) With a conditional the return is -Q + sum_w * conditional(pars) (conditional returns log P_tree), so -Q + sum_w*logP = -sum_w*(Q/sum_w - logP) and the argmin is invariant to any positive rescaling of the weights; without a conditional it is -Q as before. Added #include <limits>. No default values were introduced. Note the guard is on any non-finite loglik, not only -Inf: a +Inf loglik (the H11(a) sign defect, item 1.1) would otherwise make -Q = -Inf and nlopt would converge to that point; with the guard it is +Inf like the -Inf case.

(3) The non-finite guard covers +Inf/NaN loglik as well as -Inf (see rule_implemented).

item: 1.3 — H12, H54 (CR BDI sampler for mu0 >= lam0: .bdi_p_cr and .bdi_integral_cr in R/bdi.R)
rule_implemented: .bdi_p_cr(t, lam0, mu0, tp): computes d = lam0 - mu0; if abs(d) <= 1e-12 * max(abs(lam0), abs(mu0)) it returns the critical limit 1/(1 + lam0*(tp - t)); otherwise d / (lam0 - mu0*exp(-d*(tp - t))) as before (finite and in (0,1) for mu0 > lam0). .bdi_integral_cr(t1, t2, n, k, lam0, mu0, tp): same relative switch (1e-12 * max(|lam0|,|mu0|), replacing the old absolute 1e-15) selects the critical branch, whose integrals are now I_lam = lam0*dt - log(a1/a2) and I_mu = lam0*dt + log((tp-t1)/(tp-t2)) with a1 = 1 + lam0*(tp-t1), a2 = 1 + lam0*(tp-t2); I_mu is only computed when n > 0 (returns Inf when n > 0 and tp - t2 < 1e-300, matching the general branch; avoids 0*Inf = NaN when n = 0). In the general branch the divergence guard is now abs(oE2) < 1e-300 instead of oE2 < 1e-300, so mu0 > lam0 (where 1 - E2 < 0) gives the finite closed form. The relative tolerance 1e-12 was chosen because the general formula keeps ~1e-9 absolute accuracy at d = 1e-10 and is exact to 1e-12 at d = 1e-13 (measured), so nothing is lost by switching at 1e-12 and both functions switch at the same d. The mu0 < lam0 path is unchanged.

item: 1.4 — H10, H11(b), H59: BDI E-step rejection accounting, acceptance-corrected fhat, non-finite draw handling (R/bdi.R .augment_tree_bdi, .bdi_augment_one)
rule_implemented: .bdi_augment_one now always returns a list with $reason in {"accepted", "survivor", "max_missing"} (accepted draws also carry $species, $n_alive_at_tp, $logg); no bare NULL. .augment_tree_bdi: (1) retry budget max_tries = 5L * sample_size for every model (was sample_size under CR); (2) counts n_attempts, n_rejected (survivor channel: missing lineage alive at tp), n_rejected_max_missing (overflow channel) separately; (3) after eval_logf, completed draws with non-finite log-weight (is.finite(logf - logg) FALSE) are removed from the returned trees/logf/logg/weights (the M-step set) and counted in n_nonfinite; (4) acc = n_valid / (n_valid + n_rejected) where n_valid = all completed draws (finite + non-finite), NA_real_ if both are zero; (5) fhat = log(sum_w / n_valid) + max_lw + log(acc) with sum_w over the finite draws only, so non-finite draws sit in the denominator at weight zero and max_missing overflows are excluded from the denominator (mirrors S_completed in src/E_step.cpp); fhat = -Inf when no finite draw remains (including the all-non-finite case, which returns an empty tree set so .mcem_bdi's existing length(trees) == 0 branch treats it as an E-step failure); (6) warning(call. = FALSE) with the counts whenever n_valid < sample_size. Return list gains n_valid, n_nonfinite, n_attempts, n_rejected, n_rejected_max_missing, acc. Under CR acc = 1 and fhat is numerically unchanged (matches DDD::bd_loglik(cond=0, btorph=1, soc=2) to < 1e-8 in the test). Roxygen for both functions updated and man/ regenerated with devtools::document() (roxygen2 7.3.3 = RoxygenNote; only the two expected Rd files changed).

rule_implemented: .mcem_bdi (R/bdi.R) now does the following. (1) Stopping rule: delta_k = max_j |theta_k[j] - theta_{k-1}[j]| / max(|theta_{k-1}[j]|, eps), eps = 1e-2 (a local constant), "converged" when delta_k < tol for `patience` consecutive iterations; upper_bound - lower_bound no longer enters anywhere (range_vec and center_pars removed). The function's `tol` argument now defaults to 1e-2. Justification: on the audit's reference configuration (25-tip CR tree of H21.R, box [0,3]^2, N = 200, start near the MLE) I ran the OLD code with tol = 0 for 40 iterations and applied both rules post hoc to the same trajectory: the old range-scaled rule (1e-3 x 3) fired at iteration 5, the new rule at tol = 1e-2 fired at 6 (2e-2 at 4; 1e-3, 2e-3 and 5e-3 never fired in 40). At N = 200 the relative MC noise of an M-step iterate near the fixed point is 0.5-1.3 % (sd (0.0021, 0.0029) at (0.435, 0.226) from the audit's part A), so 1e-2 sits at the noise scale the way 3e-3 absolute did for a box of ~3x the parameter. On a 12-tip tree (larger noise) 1e-2 fired at 26 where the old rule never fired in 40. (2) An iteration whose M-step returned its start unchanged (any(new != old) is FALSE) resets the streak and is recorded with m_moved = FALSE; it never counts toward patience. (3) The trace `mcem` has columns par1..parP, fhat, delta_max, abs_step (max_j |theta_k - theta_{k-1}|), drift (relative displacement over the last `patience` iterations, NA for the first `patience` rows), m_step, m_moved, rejected (= .n0(e$n_rejected) from the E-step output, no literal), n_nonfinite (= sum(!is.finite(e$logf))), num_trees, ESS, time. Row names no longer read "elapsed…" (proc.time name stripped). (4) Draws with non-finite log-weight or logf are excluded from the tree set passed to m_cpp (weights renormalised over the finite ones; rejected_zero_weights in the e_step list = their count); an E-step with no finite draw is treated as an E-step failure. fhat is taken from .augment_tree_bdi unchanged (its definition belongs to item 1.4). rule_implemented: .mcem_dynamic_fresh now does the following. (1) Stopping rule: delta_k = max_j |theta_k,j - theta_{k-1,j}| / max(|theta_{k-1,j}|, 1e-2), measured against the point actually fed to em_cpp; "converged" after `patience` consecutive iterations with delta_k < tol; ub - lb no longer enters. Function default tol = 1e-2 (chosen because on a parameter-scale box it is roughly what the old box-scaled 1e-3 amounted to, e.g. 3e-3 abs on [0,3] for rates ~0.4; the control default tol = 1e-3 in inference.R is outside my item and untouched; .run_mcem always passes ctrl$tol so the function default only affects direct calls). Trace gains abs_step (max |dtheta|) and drift (relative displacement over the last `patience` completed iterations, NA before that). (2) Final E-step: after the loop, if at least one iteration succeeded and stop_reason != "e_step_failure", em_cpp is run once more at theta_K (its M-step estimate discarded); its fhat/logf/logg feed the trace's last row (final_estep = TRUE, delta/abs_step/drift NA), loglik_var and final_IS, so .run_mcem's tail(fhat) = fhat(theta_K) at fit$pars. If that call fails, the lagged values are kept and final_estep = FALSE. (3) maxN ratchet: on failure maxN <- max(maxN, min(2*maxN, 50000)) — never reset after a success, never reduced (the old min() shrank a user maxN > 50000); the maxN used is a trace column and the final value is returned as `maxN`. (4) Recovery: every failure resets streak to 0 and increments n_failed; the first consecutive failure retries at prev_pars (last successful M-step estimate, init before any) with the larger cap; from fail_streak >= 2 the sampling point is moved cur_pars <- clamp(0.8*cur_pars + 0.2*centre), compounding, while prev_pars is untouched. (5) Eight consecutive failures: stop_reason "e_step_failure", pars = prev_pars (init if no success), iterations = n_success (0L in the all-fail case, an integer, never NULL), n_failed returned, .mcem_warn_estep called at prev_pars, mcem/final_IS NULL and loglik_var NA when nothing succeeded. (6) Rejection columns: rejected, rejected_overruns, rejected_lambda, rejected_zero_weights and n_rejected = rejected + overruns + lambda, the same sum final_IS$n_rejected uses; the verbose line prints n_rejected. Return list: mcem, pars, iterations, n_failed, stop_reason, final_estep, maxN, loglik_var, final_IS.

item: 1.7 — H1, H16 (E-step half), H62, H68: thinning E-step acceptance rule, stop-flag race, fhat denominator, num_trees exposure
rule_implemented: In E_step() (src/E_step.cpp): each worker checks `stop` at the top of every iteration and breaks; after augmenting and scoring, it takes the mutex FIRST, re-checks `stop` under the lock and breaks if set (nothing stored, nothing counted after stop); then `if (std::isfinite(log_w)) { if (trees.size() < N) { push tree/weight/logf/logg; if (trees.size() == N) stop = true; } } else if (log_w == -Inf) ++rejected_zero_weights; else ++rejected_nonfinite;`. `stop` is only ever assigned true (also the 120 s time-budget write is now under the lock). The three catch blocks take the lock, break if stop is set, and otherwise increment their counter. fhat denominator is `S_completed = trees.size() + rejected_zero_weights` (was `N + rzw`). The `0.0 < std::exp(log_w)` clause is gone, so any finite log-weight is accepted regardless of magnitude (lw of -960 accepted in the test). New field `int rejected_nonfinite = 0` in E_step_info_t (inst/include/emphasis.hpp) and a "non-finite weights" term in the emphasis_error_E message. Both Rcpp wrappers (augment_trees / em_cpp) now return `rejected_nonfinite` and `num_trees` (= E.info.num_trees, i.e. trees.size()); em_cpp's existing `trees` (count when copy_trees = FALSE) is unchanged. No default values were chosen; the semantics of -Inf = zero-weight tree (enters the fhat denominator) and +Inf/NaN = invalid draw (excluded from the denominator, like overruns/lambda) follow the plan.

rule_implemented: In do_augment_tree_cont (src/augment_tree.cpp): (1) the start-of-segment rate is model.nh_rate evaluated at std::nextafter(cbt, next_bt), so lower_bound inside nh_rate selects the segment's node — the one upper_bound(cbt) returns, carrying the post-event count — while the survival factor is unchanged to machine precision (helper segment_start_rate). (2) constant_rates = (pars[2]==0 && pars[3]==0 && pars[6]==0 && pars[7]==0): lambda and mu then depend on n only, so nh(t) = n_seg*lambda*(1 - rho*exp(-mu_eff*(T-t))) is decreasing on the segment and the envelope is Lambda* = nh(cbt+) = n_seg*lambda*(1 - rho*exp(-mu_eff*(T-cbt))) (mu_eff = max(mu,1e-10) comes from nh_rate). Otherwise (M or D coefficient active, rates vary within the segment) Lambda* = envelope_safety * max(nh(cbt+), nh(next_bt)) with envelope_safety = 2.0 (a named constant; chosen because the endpoint maximum is off by at most the ratio of lambda's or the survival factor's change across a segment, which is below 2 for moderate coefficients — a heuristic, so the counter is the diagnostic). (3) The envelope is computed once per segment (flag new_interval) and held after a rejected candidate; it is recomputed only after an accepted insertion or when next_bt is reached — no collapse to nh(next_bt). (4) pt = nh(t*)/Lambda*; if pt > 1 + 1e-12 (pt_tolerance, rounding allowance between two exp() evaluations) an std::atomic<long long> envelope_violations is incremented; pt is then clipped to 1 (no throw: a violation is recorded, not turned into a rejection). item: 1.9 — H35 (n_pars), H21/H12 (default init), H22 part A (maxN check), H31 (stop_reason/iterations + print)
commit: 9007ecc (parent f5f51ce, the same base as main and the other wave-1 worktrees)
rule_implemented: (1) estimate_rates: n_pars <- sum(lower_bound != upper_bound) on the compact scale; AIC = -2*loglik + 2*n_pars uses it, so a dd fit with gamma_N fixed (lb == ub) reports n_pars = 3. (2) Default MCEM init (init_pars = NULL): after the existing midpoint + slope-to-zero step, if init_pars[1] (beta_0) == init_pars[j_mu] (gamma_0, j_mu = length/2 + 1), gamma_0 is set to 0.5*beta_0 (exponential link: beta_0 - log 2; gaussian: 0.5*beta_0 too) and clamped to [lb, ub] of gamma_0. If it still equals beta_0 after clamping AND ctrl$sampling == "bdi" AND .bdi_supported(model, link), stop() with a message naming the two parameters, the value and the mu bounds and asking for init_pars with lambda != mu. The thinning sampler (and non-BDI models/links) is left to start at lambda == mu because it can. User-supplied init_pars are never altered. (3) estimate_rates_control("mcem")$maxN is now NULL (was 2000L), so the existing .run_mcem fallback max(2000L, 10L * sample_size) applies; after that resolution .run_mcem stop()s with call. = FALSE when ctrl$maxN < ctrl$sample_size, regardless of sampler (the documented invariant is general; only the thinning sampler reads maxN). Roxygen for maxN and the hand-written man/estimate_rates_control.Rd line updated accordingly. (4) .run_mcem returns stop_reason = raw$stop_reason and iterations = if (is.null(raw$mcem)) 0L else nrow(raw$mcem); estimate_rates copies them to the top level of the fit (NA_character_/NA_integer_ for cem/gam, whose runners were not touched). print.emphasis_fit prints "Iterations:" and "Stop reason:" when non-NA, and when loglik is NA adds "Did not converge (<stop_reason>): no log-likelihood was obtained; the parameters above are not estimates." Return-value roxygen documents stop_reason and iterations.
deviations: The worktree was created from d9ca72a (the remote's default branch `debug`, no R/inference.R, no tests/) instead of f5f51ce like the other wave-1 worktrees; I ran `git reset --hard f5f51ce` on my own branch before touching anything, so the commit's parent is f5f51ce. Beyond that: the lambda == mu error is restricted to the BDI-supported case rather than unconditional (thinning starts fine at lambda == mu, verified in the test file); and I corrected one line of the hand-written man/estimate_rates_control.Rd (default 2000 -> NULL) because it would otherwise contradict the new default — that page also still says the default sampling is "dynamic_fresh", which was already stale and I left it.
